drivingQuestion: Why is a piece of forbidden meat not nullified by the permitted majority, and on what construal does Rav's ruling about a piece becoming carrion hold?
outcomeNote: The significance difficulty is answered by ראויה להתכבד, and Rav Safra's difficulty on Rav is answered twice — by Abaye's restriction to a case where the piece was removed first, and by Rava's construal of the pot as a type with its own type and something else. Rav's ruling stands on both.

segments.he: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר, כֹּל שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לִימָּנוֹת שָׁנִינוּ, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֶת שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לִימָּנוֹת שָׁנִינוּ, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר? שָׁאנֵי חֲתִיכָה, הוֹאִיל וּרְאוּיָה לְהִתְכַּבֵּד בָּהּ לִפְנֵי הָאוֹרְחִים.
segments.en: The Gemara clarifies its challenge. «This» ruling «works out well according to the one who said» that «we learned: Any» item «whose manner is to be counted,» i.e., that is sometimes sold by unit rather than by weight or volume, is considered significant and therefore is not subject to nullification. «But according to the one who said» that «we learned:» It is only an item «whose manner is» exclusively «to be counted,» i.e., that is always sold by unit, that is considered significant, and is therefore not subject to nullification, «what can be said?» Since pieces of meat or fish are not always sold by unit, they should be subject to nullification. The Gemara answers: «A piece» of meat or fish «is different, since it is suitable to give honor with it» by placing it «before guests.» Therefore, due to its significance it is not subject to nullification.

segments.he: וּצְרִיכָא, דְּאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן גִּיד – מִשּׁוּם דִּבְרִיָּה הִיא, אֲבָל חֲתִיכָה – אֵימָא לָא.
segments.en: The Gemara adds: «And» it was «necessary» for the mishna to teach both the halakha that the sciatic nerve is not nullified and the halakha that a piece of non-kosher meat or fish is not nullified, «as if» the mishna had «taught us» only the case of a sciatic «nerve,» one might think that it is not nullified «because it is» a distinct «entity, but» in the case of «a piece» of non-kosher meat, «say» it is «not» significant, and it is subject to nullification.

segments.he: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן חֲתִיכָה, הוֹאִיל וּרְאוּיָה לְהִתְכַּבֵּד בָּהּ לִפְנֵי הָאוֹרְחִים, אֲבָל גִּיד – אֵימָא לָא. צְרִיכָא.
segments.en: «And if» the mishna had «taught us» the halakha only in the case of «a piece» of non-kosher meat or fish, one might think that it is not nullified «since it is suitable to give honor with it» by placing it «before the guests. But» in the case of a sciatic «nerve, say» it is «not» significant, and it is subject to nullification. Therefore it was «necessary» for the mishna to teach both cases.

segments.he: דָּרֵשׁ רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: חֲתִיכָה שֶׁל נְבֵלָה וְשֶׁל דָּג טָמֵא אֵינָהּ אוֹסֶרֶת, עַד שֶׁתִּתֵּן טַעַם בָּרוֹטֶב וּבַקֵּיפֶה וּבַחֲתִיכוֹת.
segments.en: § «Rabba bar bar Ḥana taught: A piece» of meat «of an unslaughtered carcass or of a non-kosher» species of «fish» that fell into a pot of kosher food «does not render» the contents of the pot «forbidden unless it imparts flavor to the broth and to the deposits» of food remaining in the pot «and to the» other «pieces» of food in the pot.

segments.he: אוֹקֵי רַב אָמוֹרָא עֲלֵיהּ, וּדְרַשׁ: כֵּיוָן שֶׁנָּתַן טַעַם בַּחֲתִיכָה – חֲתִיכָה עַצְמָהּ נַעֲשֵׂת נְבֵלָה, וְאוֹסֶרֶת כׇּל הַחֲתִיכוֹת כּוּלָּן מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מִינָהּ.
segments.en: «Rav» disagreed with Rabba bar bar Ḥana and «appointed a disseminator» to stand «before him» and teach his statement to a wider audience, «and» he «taught: Once» the non-kosher meat or fish «has imparted flavor to» another «piece» in the pot, that second «piece itself becomes non-kosher. And» this second piece «renders all the pieces» of meat or fish in the pot «forbidden, because they are» of the same «type;» therefore, nullification does not apply.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סָפְרָא לְאַבָּיֵי: מִכְּדֵי רַב כְּמַאן אַמְרַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתֵּיהּ? כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר מִין בְּמִינוֹ לֹא בָּטֵיל. מַאי אִירְיָא כִּי נָתַן טַעַם? אֲפִילּוּ כִּי לֹא נָתַן טַעַם נָמֵי! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן – בְּשֶׁקָּדַם וְסִלְּקוֹ.
segments.en: «Rav Safra said to Abaye: Now, in accordance with whose» opinion did «Rav say his statement?» It is «in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Yehuda, who says» that «a type» of food mixed «with» food of «its» own «type is not nullified.» But if so, «why» does Rav state «specifically that» the non-kosher meat renders all the pieces forbidden only «when it» has «imparted flavor» to another piece? «Even if it did not impart flavor» to another piece it should render all the contents of the pot forbidden. Abaye «said to him: Here we are dealing with» a case «where he» cooked the non-kosher piece with one kosher piece and «first removed» the non-kosher piece before adding the other pieces. Consequently, the remaining pieces are forbidden only if the non-kosher piece imparted flavor to the piece it was cooked with.
«Rava said» an alternate answer to Rav Safra’s challenge of Rav’s statement:

segments.he: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא לֹא קָדַם וְסִלְּקוֹ, הָוֵי מִין וּמִינוֹ וְדָבָר אַחֵר.
segments.en: «You» may «even say» that it is referring to a case where «he did not first remove» the piece of non-kosher meat or fish. Nevertheless, this «is» a case of a mixture of one «type» of food «with» its «own type» of food «and» with «something else,» i.e., the spices and broth in the pot.

segments.he: וְכׇל מִין וּמִינוֹ וְדָבָר אַחֵר – סַלֵּק אֶת מִינוֹ כְּמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ, וְשֶׁאֵין מִינוֹ רָבֶה עָלָיו וּמְבַטְּלוֹ.
segments.en: «And» in «any» case of «a type» of forbidden food mixed with «its own type» of food «and» with «something else, disregard» the food that is «its own type, as though it is not» present in the mixture, «and» if the amount of permitted food «that is not its own type is» sixty times «greater than» the forbidden food, the permitted food «nullifies it.» Rav’s ruling applies to a case where the forbidden piece of meat or fish imparts flavor to another piece before the spices and broth are added, and there is a total volume sixty times greater than the original non-kosher piece. Consequently, even if the amount of spices and broth is eventually sixty times greater than the original non-kosher piece of meat or fish, the entire mixture is forbidden, as the spices and broth are not sixty times greater than the two pieces of meat or fish which are now non-kosher.

moves.summary: the non-nullification works only on the lenient reading of the significance rule; on the strict reading it fails
moves.about: the mishna's non-nullification of a forbidden piece works only for the view that anything sometimes counted individually is significant; on the stricter view a piece of meat should be nullified

moves.summary: a piece is different, being fit to serve with honor before guests
moves.about: answering its own difficulty — a piece of meat is significant even on the stricter view, since it is fit to be served with honor before guests

moves.summary: the nerve case alone would not have yielded the piece case, since the nerve is significant only as a beriya
moves.about: why the mishna had to teach both the sciatic nerve and the piece of carcass — neither case could be derived from the other, since the nerve is significant as a beriya and the piece as fit to honor guests

moves.summary: nor would the piece case have yielded the nerve case; both were necessary
expounds that a forbidden piece forbids only once it imparts flavor to broth, sediment and pieces
moves.about: whether a forbidden piece forbids the mixture only once it imparts flavor to broth, sediment and pieces alike, or already once it imparts flavor to a single piece, which then itself becomes carrion

moves.summary: Rav counter-expounds through a disseminator: the piece that absorbed the flavor itself becomes carrion and forbids the rest
moves.about: Rav stations a disseminator before him to broadcast his ruling against Rabba bar bar Ḥana's

moves.summary: if Rav follows R' Yehuda, why did he require that flavor was imparted at all
moves.about: in accordance with whose view Rav stated his ruling

moves.summary: Rav spoke where the forbidden piece was removed before the others were added
moves.about: answering Rav Safra's difficulty on Rav by restricting the case to one where the forbidden piece was removed first

moves.summary: Rava offers a competing answer to the same difficulty
moves.about: an alternative answer to Rav Safra's difficulty: even without removing the forbidden piece, the pot is a case of a type with its own type plus something else

moves.summary: even without removing the piece, this is a type with its own type and something else
moves.about: how Rav's ruling is to be construed so that it fits R' Yehuda's principle — Abaye restricts it to a case where the forbidden piece was removed first, Rava does not

moves.summary: states the governing rule: disregard the like type, and only the unlike type can nullify
moves.about: construing Rav's ruling as a mixture of a type with its own type and something else, where the like type is disregarded and only the unlike type can nullify
